assumptions: Estimated continuation of the original launch, payload and entry state. Starts the three healthy sea-level Raptors during a physical flip at 1.1 km, the broadcast ignition (T+03:08:10 shows 1.2 km at 363 km/h; the landing burn starts at T+03:08:11). The braking target is two constant-deceleration segments calibrated to the broadcast displays: 7 m/s2 through 0.8 km/363 km/h and 0.3 km/203 km/h, then 1.045 m/s2 from 15 m/s at 100 m to 4 m/s at the water (the 60 km/h display near the end, within its unspecified altitude datum and rounding). The flip had sat at 0.6 km only while the crossflow drag was the subcritical 1.5 coefficient and the belly flop fell at ~65 m/s instead of the observed ~101 m/s. It then reduces selected engine count monotonically as thrust demand falls. Uses existing engine/gimbal/flap, shutdown/startup and tank-consumption models. This controller explicitly bounds actual start-attempt counters against engine-model restart metadata; the generic runtime does not enforce that metadata. A first 100 m descending gate is a terminal-burn diagnostic, not water contact or mission acceptance. Powered-descent vector guidance: the vertical channel tracks the profile with its deceleration as feed-forward, the horizontal channel damps drift at 0.2/s inside a 30 deg tilt cone (35-40 deg lost attitude on one engine), and the minimum-thrust surplus of the lit Raptors is steered into drift braking. Engines are selected for 80% throttle headroom and a 2x gimbal-moment margin over the predicted aerodynamic moment, which reproduces the observed three-two-one sequence; the flip uses a lower rate-damping gain so it turns at the gimbal-limited rate. The 100 m diagnostic gate allows 20 m/s total (broadcast 60 km/h near the end). Gains, tilt and margins are estimates; the lateral (tilt-to-kill-drift) loop gain is 0.2/s so it stays several times slower than the single-engine attitude loop (0.5/s limit-cycled ±11° near 100 m); clocks do not command the trajectory. Burns the original header-tank propellant; the main-tank residual was vented before entry. No resources are created or refilled. No measured SpaceX bank schedule, throttle or landing coordinates are asserted. Gameplay optionally continues beyond the retained 100 m diagnostic to a bounded Pacific open-water region (22.3..35 N, 161..140 W), a geographic operating domain rather than measured targeting coordinates. NOAA ETOPO 2022 native 15 arc-second screening of all 15,361,920 cells in this rectangle gives elevations from -7024 to -66.55 m, with no missing cells; see docs/research/FLIGHT14_OCEAN_COVERAGE_2026-11-06.json. This relocates the water model coverage after descent recalibration; contact-speed, attitude, propellant and water-load limits are unchanged. Lowest exposed vacuum nozzle follows the current visible skirt datum at -3.78 m. Water loads approximate a sealed cylinder clipped by the local sea plane at its actual inclination, with sectional cross-flow drag and separate axial nozzle drag with seawater density 1025 kg/m3 and drag coefficient 0.8, not slamming CFD, flooding or waves. Cutoff follows actual nozzle contact, then ten seconds of mass-centred coupled water response are integrated before the preview freezes. Early heeling is a sealed-hull engineering estimate, not validated recovery or measured flooding/capsize timing. Physical wave displacement is zero; visual ripples do not move the contact surface. The verified all-ocean operating domain was extended south by 0.2 degree after F4 corrected transport and ignition behavior; this changes geographic coverage, not steering or contact acceptance. An additional disjoint ocean rectangle (20..22 N, 164..162 W) covers the westward original-profile crossing; NOAA ETOPO 2022 screens all 230,400 native cells with elevations -5307..-1786.89 m. The domain is the union of the three verified rectangles, not their enclosing box; island exclusions and physical contact limits remain unchanged. A separate rectangle east of Kauai (22..22.3 N, 159..158 W) is also verified: all 17,280 native cells have elevations -4927.50..-1692.27 m. It covers the propagated isolated and moving-world crossings after routed flow momentum is conserved through fragmentation. The nearby island and unscreened gaps remain excluded. An adjoining rectangle north of Oahu (22..22.3 N, 158..157.5 W) is verified the same way: all 8,640 native cells have elevations -4936.96..-3970.32 m. It covers the moving-world crossing after the Kepler-world integration frame began accelerating with the Moon's pull on Earth (tides only); Oahu stays outside.
